Declare the coefficients of a model

Source: R/specify_coefs.R
declare_coefs.Rd

declare_coefs() makes a set of coefficients for the terms of a model: one value for each column that the specification builds on a network. A set of coefficients gives the initial values of an estimation, or the model that simulate() draws networks from.

It is a generic, with a method for each model:

  • for a specification from specify_mrqap(), the values stated in ...;

  • for an infernetMrqapFit, from estimate_mrqap(), the estimated coefficients, with the specification, the family, and the residual standard deviation of the fit.

A coefficient is the estimated or stated value of a model's term. A value that is not stated is NA.

Usage

declare_coefs(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
declare_coefs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_formula'
declare_coefs(x, ..., family = NULL, sigma = NULL, .data = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
declare_coefs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapCoefs'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'infernetMrqapFit'
coef(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A specification from specify_mrqap(), or a fitted model, such as an infernetMrqapFit from estimate_mrqap().

...

For a specification, the values of the coefficients, each named for its column, such as "(Intercept)" = -2, ego_age = 0.1, or as one named vector, such as stats::coef(fit). For a fit, not used.

family

The family of the model: "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negbin", or "zip", as in control_mrqap(). NULL, the default, reads it from the values of the outcome in .data, as estimate_mrqap() does: "binomial" for a 0/1 outcome, "poisson" for a count, and "gaussian" for any other (see control_mrqap()). Without .data, NULL aborts.

sigma

For a "gaussian" model, the standard deviation of the residuals. Other families do not use it.

.data

Optionally, the network that the specification builds its columns on, to check the names of the values.

object

A set of coefficients from declare_coefs(), or an infernetMrqapFit from estimate_mrqap().

Value

An object of class infernetMrqapCoefs: a named numeric vector of the coefficients, with NA for a value that is not stated. Its attributes are spec, the specification; family, the family; and sigma, the standard deviation of the residuals, or NULL. Printing it gives the family, the formula, and the values. stats::coef() gives the values as a plain named vector. stats::coef() of an infernetMrqapFit gives its estimated coefficients the same way, so coef(declare_coefs(fit)) equals coef(fit).

Details

The names of the values are the names of the columns that the specification builds, as estimate_mrqap() names its coefficients: "(Intercept)", and then a column such as "ego_age" or "same_dept". summary(specify_mrqap(formula, .data), .data) lists the columns of each term in its columns column. With .data, declare_coefs() checks each name against these columns, and gives each column without a value an NA. Without it, the names are checked when simulate() builds the columns.

simulate() reads a set of coefficients of a "gaussian", "binomial", or "poisson" model. A "gaussian" model also needs sigma, the standard deviation of its residuals, also where the family was read from the outcome. estimate_mrqap() uses a set of coefficients as initial values where its estimator iterates.

See also

simulate_mrqap to simulate networks from a set of coefficients, and estimate_mrqap() for the initial values of an estimation.

Other specifying functions: declare_coefs_ergm, specify_ergm(), specify_mrqap(), specify_saom(), specify_terms, terms_mrqap

Examples

spec <- specify_mrqap(friends ~ social + tasks)
coefs <- declare_coefs(spec, "(Intercept)" = -1.5, social = 0.2,
                       tasks = -0.4, family = "poisson",
                       .data = ison_algebra)
coefs
#> # Coefficients of a poisson MRQAP
#> # 3 of 3 coefficients stated
#> 
#> friends ~ social + tasks
#> 
#> (Intercept)      social       tasks 
#>        -1.5         0.2        -0.4 
stats::coef(coefs)
#> (Intercept)      social       tasks 
#>        -1.5         0.2        -0.4 

# The coefficients of a fit
fit <- estimate_mrqap(friends ~ social + tasks, ison_algebra, times = 5,
                      control = list(family = "poisson"))
declare_coefs(fit)
#> # Coefficients of a poisson MRQAP
#> # 3 of 3 coefficients stated
#> 
#> friends ~ social + tasks
#> 
#> (Intercept)      social       tasks 
#>  -1.6058039   0.2325937  -0.4087764
